Past Tense Review: Simple Past, Present Perfect and Past Continuous
You use the Simple Past , the Past Continuous and the Present Perfect to talk about the past. Each of these tense has their own use.

You use the Simple Past:
to talk about past actions which are over at the time of speaking
Example: I heard from the neighbors that there is going to be road work next week.

to talk about past states
Example: I lived in a different neighborhood when I was a kid.

You use the Past Continuous:
to talk about being in the middle of a situation - there will probably be an interruption (Simple Past) in the sentence.
Example: Everything was going smoothly when Jill took over the project.

You use the Present Perfect to:
talk about actions that finished recently for which there is a present result
Example: The office has bought everyone a new computer.

talk about actions that started in the past and are still happening
Example: I've worked here for 10 years.

talk about experiences in your life or events in history
Example: I've never been to Italy.

Peter: The first word is E-G-G-O-N. The blizzard has started to let up a little. The wind has begun to calm down as well. Look at that couple over there.
Amy: They're having a row.
Vanessa: She's running out and he's following her. I wonder what happened?
Peter: Hmmm. I'll play along. He must have forgotten his wallet and then asked her to pay.

Vanessa: She might have had plans to go to the opera tonight and the weather ruined them.
Peter: Meh. The weather was bad. Consequently, they couldn't go to the opera? Not your best, V.
Vanessa: It's just as good as your “Godzilla may have stepped on the city” routine.
Amy: I was actually watching before. I think the girl was angry because the guy might have dated the server.
Vanessa: How did you know?

Amy: The server and the guy were giving each other looks throughout the evening. The girl in the argument must have known about it.
Peter: She could have known. She raised such turmoil just now that I think maybe she had known and just snapped.
Vanessa: He reminds me of Vincent. Have you ever met Vincent, Peter?
Peter: Yeah, I've met Vincent.
Amy: Who's Vincent?
Vanessa: He worked as a bartender part-time at the Bistro. Apparently, once he was dating two girls at the same time and one night they were all at the same party together. He said he was running around the party trying to avoid them.
Amy: What happened?
Vanessa: Yep!

Amy: What happened?
Vanessa: He said the two girls were yelling and screaming a lot and at one point the police were called. I didn't hear what happened after that.
Amy: That's why I prefer nice boys.
Peter: This has been a great night.
Vanessa: I'm having a great time too. This place has served as such a cozy little shelter. I'm enjoying the ambiance and the company and a double-letter score. S-A-V-I-O-U-R ... used all my tiles as well. For this reason, I get a bonus.
Amy: Well played, Vanessa.
Vanessa: Who is superior now, Peter?
Amy: I don't know Vanessa.
Peter: What is quartzy?
Vanessa: It means resembling quartz and it means we might be in big trouble.
